headline: Add PKCE to Google sign-in
summary: The Google authorization-code flow now uses PKCE, binding each authorization request to a session-side verifier.

items.title: Add PKCE to the Google authorization-code flow
items.body: Google sign-in now sends a PKCE code_challenge (S256 method) on the authorization request and presents the matching code_verifier — held only in the server-side session — at token exchange, per OAuth 2.1 and RFC 9700. An authorization code intercepted between Google and the callback can no longer be redeemed without the session's verifier, closing the authorization-code-injection vector that state alone does not cover. The token and userinfo requests also now surface a non-2xx response as the true HTTP status instead of parsing an error body as a success payload.
